**Key Visual Observations:**

- Banana fruit bunch on a standing plant
- Prominent **blackening and shriveling at the distal tips** (blossom/perianth end) of multiple banana fingers
- The affected tips appear **dry, corrugated, and darkened** — progressing inward from the tip
- The stem/rachis shows browning consistent with infection spread
- Leaves in the background appear healthy (no leaf spots, no bunchy top)

**Reasoning Through Classes:**

- **Cigar End Rot**: The blackening originates at the perianth/tip end and the tissue appears dry and shrunken — this is the textbook description: *"infection spreads from the perianth to the fingers, causing blackening of the skin, shrinkage and folding of tissues... resembling ash on a cigar end."* The visual matches precisely.
- **Anthracnose**: Would show sunken black lesions across the fruit surface, typically post-harvest — not concentrated at tips.
- **Panama Disease**: Causes whole-plant wilting/death — plant here is upright and productive.
- **Banana_Bunchy_Top_Virus / Bunchy_Top**: Affects leaf shape (stunted, erect, marginal chlorosis) — leaves here are normal.
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka / Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Leaf diseases — no fruit tip involvement.

The blackened, dry, corrugated tips of the banana fingers spreading inward from the perianth is the hallmark of **Cigar End Rot**.
